title: Not in our hands (Avot 4:15)
hook: the corner-cutter gets promoted, the careful one gets the bad news: Yannai says we cannot explain it
tomorrow: she beat you. do you say hi first?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Rabbi Nehorai: exile yourself to a place of Torah; it won't come after you. Go where learning is. Today, a question nobody answers.
screen: `GO WHERE LEARNING IS.` → `A QUESTION NOBODY ANSWERS.`

segments.voice: Is there an answer for why? The one who cut corners gets the promotion. The one who did everything right gets the bad news. Sometimes it's small, the wrong show picked, the wrong name called. Sometimes it's the biggest question there is. Pirkei Avot has been handing out answers for weeks: do this, don't do that. And then Rabbi Yannai steps up, and for once, Avot doesn't give one.
screen: `THE CORNER-CUTTER WINS.` → `IS THERE AN ANSWER FOR WHY?` → `AVOT, FOR ONCE, DOESN'T GIVE ONE.`

segments.voice: Here's Rabbi Yannai, in plain words. It is not in our hands, neither the ease of the wicked nor the suffering of the righteous. That's the puzzle. A book of answers, and here's a saying that refuses to answer. Why keep it? Because the question is older than Avot, and the Bible doesn't hide it. The prophet Jeremiah asks God out loud: "Wherefore doth the way of the wicked prosper?" Job asks it for chapters. Yannai sits in that line of honest askers, and he says what they found: we can't explain it. Commentators even read his words two ways. Some hear: we can't explain why it happens. Others hear: we don't have the ease of the wicked, and we may not be spared the suffering of the righteous either. Either reading, he doesn't make up a reason. He doesn't say the good are secretly being punished, or that the winners secretly lost. He refuses the easy answer that would hurt someone. And notice what's still in our hands, all around this saying: how we judge, how we greet, how we honor people. Avot doesn't stop acting because one question has no answer. It holds the question and keeps going. Not in our hands.
screen: `A BOOK OF ANSWERS, AND ONE REFUSAL.` · `JEREMIAH ASKED IT TOO.` · `NO MADE-UP REASON.` · `HOLD THE QUESTION. KEEP GOING.` · then, large: `NOT IN OUR HANDS.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes, and let one question come up that has no answer for you right now: something unfair, something you can't explain. Don't answer it, and don't push it away. Just hold it, the way you'd hold a stone in an open hand, for the rest of the sit.
screen: `ONE QUESTION WITH NO ANSWER.` · `DON'T ANSWER IT.` · `HOLD IT IN AN OPEN HAND.`

segments.voice: Not in our hands. Rabbi Yannai: we cannot explain the ease of the wicked or the suffering of the righteous.
Keep this one: not in our hands, said honestly, without a made-up reason. Thirty-eight of sixty, held.

screen: `DAY 1465 COUNTS.` → `AVOT, CHAPTERS 3–6 · 38 OF 60.` → `TOMORROW: SHE BEAT YOU. DO YOU SAY HI FIRST?`

howItsDone: In Jewish mourning and comfort, visitors are taught not to explain a loss to the mourner, and many simply sit with them; the question of why the righteous suffer is studied in Job and argued in the Talmud without one settled answer.

notes: 2026-10-15 v3 (recipe v3): puzzle shape (a book of answers keeps one saying that refuses to answer). Avot 4:15a paraphrased (Rabbi Yannai: ein b'yadeinu, lo mishalvat haresha'im v'af lo miyisurei hatzadikim).

Two readings of 'ein b'yadeinu' presented as 'commentators read it two ways' (e.g. Rambam/Bartenura: not in our power to explain; others: we have neither the tranquility of the wicked nor are we spared the suffering of the righteous). Confirm both are fairly put.
Jeremiah 12:1 quoted from JPS 1917 ('Wherefore doth the way of the wicked prosper?'); the same words appear in the KJV. Verify exact JPS 1917 wording.
